tagline: Round the Horn of the Leelanau, by dune and fish shanty.
intro: M-22 comes up out of Manistee County along the Lake Michigan shore, past Arcadia and Frankfort and through the Sleeping Bear Dunes, then rounds the Leelanau Peninsula by Leland and Northport and comes down the bay side through Suttons Bay to Traverse City. The old loop was called Going Round the Horn. Built in 1913, it was the first state highway in Leelanau, Benzie and Manistee counties.

The climate along the lake suits orchards and vineyards, and farm stands and cideries line the way. The highway's marker has become a symbol of the region and a popular thing to steal. In 2016 MDOT began taking the M off some of the signs.

moments.title: Point Betsie Lighthouse
moments.text: Finished in 1858 at the southern entrance to the Manitou Passage, it was the last lighthouse on Lake Michigan to keep a keeper, until 1983.

moments.title: Sleeping Bear Dunes
moments.text: Dunes about 450 feet tall above the lake. At the Dune Climb people go up for a view of Glen Lake and run back down.

moments.title: Fishtown
moments.text: Weathered shanties, smokehouses and fish tugs on the Leland River, one of the few commercial fishing complexes left on the Great Lakes. Since 2020 some shanties have been raised above record high water.
